title: A year of thinkers

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was schools close: the tour left with specific thanks, the way Marcus Aurelius began. Your line was thank you.

A bookshelf, four spines. A slim old Chinese book of short chapters. A thick French book of essays that wander. Two Americans who lived in the same small Massachusetts town, one a lecturer, one who went to the woods. This year of the path began with them, long before the science and the schools of practice. Year four is closing, and the next days look back over it, one part at a time. Today, the four thinkers, and a hard challenge: a year of reading, and you keep one line from each.
screen: `A BOOKSHELF, FOUR SPINES.` → `YEAR FOUR IS CLOSING.` → `ONE LINE FROM EACH.`

segments.voice: Start with Lao Tzu, and the opening of the Tao Te Ching, in Legge's translation: "The Tao that can be trodden is not the enduring and unchanging Tao." The book begins by admitting that whatever it says will fall short. A strange way to open a book, and an honest one: the Way is bigger than any description of it, including this one. Then Montaigne, in France, who turned the honesty on himself. His question, in French: "Que sais-je?" What do I know? Not a sneer at knowledge. A habit of checking. Montaigne wrote about his kidney stones, his cat, his fears, his friend, and kept asking what he actually knew. Then Emerson, the lecturer, in Self-Reliance: "Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string." After Montaigne's doubt, a different note: there's something in you worth listening to. Emerson didn't mean ignore everyone. He meant don't hand your whole inner life to someone else's opinion. And Thoreau, who went to Walden Pond to live deliberately, and came back with two words: "Simplify, simplify." Our life, he said, is frittered away by detail. Set the four side by side and you can hear a kind of conversation. The Way is bigger than words. I may not know as much as I think. Something in me is still worth trusting. And it's easier to hear when life is simpler.

segments.voice: Bring back each thinker, one per few breaths, and let one line come: Lao Tzu's opening, or water, the valley, the uncarved wood; Montaigne's question, or friendship, or dancing when you dance; Emerson's trust, circles, the over-soul; Thoreau's simplify, the different drummer, the morning. Don't search; let the line that comes first be the one.
A year of thinkers. Year four's teachers: Lao Tzu, Montaigne, Emerson and Thoreau, each kept now in a single line. Today's word.
Your line: four lines. Four voices, one year. Rest well, and I'll see you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some readers of Lao Tzu, Montaigne, Emerson and Thoreau keep a commonplace book, copying short lines from each into one notebook and returning to them over time.

chat.says: Of all those thinkers this year, what did each one teach you?
options: The Way is bigger than words; what do I know?; trust thyself; and simplify, simplify.
That doubt is useless, books can't help, and the woods beat any town for living.
All four said the same thing: people should trust experts over themselves.
chat.meaning: Lao Tzu: the Tao beyond words. Montaigne: what do I know? Emerson: trust thyself. Thoreau: simplify, simplify. Four voices, four lines.
